title: Designing a lesson with measurable outcomes

questions.q: In "Outcomes and Bloom verbs", which of these is a key idea?
o: Read it against your checklist.
Use the Year 7 science case card.
Replace know and understand with identify, list or calculate.
Order activities from easy to hard.

questions.q: In "Alignment: outcome, activity, check", which of these is a key idea?
o: Each check matches an outcome.
Read it against your checklist.
Add one activity and one check for each.
Draft a lesson with two to four outcomes.

questions.q: In "Designing a 5-item check", which of these is a key idea?
o: Start each outcome with an action verb you can observe (a Bloom verb comes from a standard list of thinking verbs).
One correct answer per item.
Note the verbs you used.
Plan one change for your next lesson.

questions.q: In "Timing and flow", which of these is a key idea?
o: Use the Year 7 science case card.
Add a measure such as 4 of 5.
Review a peer's plan with a checklist.
Order activities from easy to hard.

questions.q: In "Practice: draft your lesson", which of these is a key idea?
o: Leave time for the check.
Add one activity and one check for each.
Note the verbs you used.
Check the verbs.

questions.q: In "Peer feedback and assessment", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep your best lesson plan.
Review a peer's plan with a checklist.
Order activities from easy to hard.
Note the verbs you used.

questions.q: In "Second worked case", which of these is a key idea?
o: Each activity leads to one outcome.
Give each activity a time.
Leave time for the check.
Write three outcomes and one check each.

questions.q: In "Portfolio and reflection", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep your best lesson plan.
Add one activity and one check for each.
Give two strengths and one improvement.
If few learners meet the outcome, re-teach and re-check.
